title: Finite-generator subsheaf stages with joint stalk coverage
statement: Let $X$ have a basis of quasi-compact opens and let $F$ be an abelian sheaf [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Let $S=\coprod_{U\subseteq X\text{ open quasi-compact}} F(U)$. There is a functor $D:\operatorname{Finset}(S)\to\operatorname{Ab}(X)$ and a cocone $c:D\to F$ whose maps are monomorphisms and jointly surjective on every stalk: for each $x$ and $t\in F_x$ there are $A\in\operatorname{Finset}(S)$ and $s\in(D_A)_x$ with $(c_A)_x(s)=t$. Each $D_A$ admits an epimorphism from a finite coproduct of $E_U=j_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_U$, where all indexing opens are quasi-compact, allowing an empty coproduct. The constant sheaf and extension by zero are [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and [def-sc-abelian-open-extension-by-zero]; stalks are [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

source.place: Lemma 02UX (lemma-vanishing-generated-one-section), first paragraph of the proof

proof.text: For each compact-open section s construct E_U to F by the constant sheaf adjunction, multiplication by s, and the extension-by-zero counit. The distinguished integer-1 germ maps to s_x.

For each finite set A form the finite coproduct of its generators and take the image of its map to F. Abelian image factorization yields the monic inclusion and epic presentation. Enumerate A by Fin A.card.
For A contained in B, use the commuting square of coproducts over F to induce the image inclusion. Uniqueness under the monic inclusion proves identity and composition laws and cocone compatibility.

Represent a germ on an open neighborhood, then restrict to a compact basis open. The singleton stage for this restricted section contains the germ by the integer-1 formula. This gives the asserted joint stalk coverage, with no claim yet that F is the colimit.

mathlib_searches.query: directed colimit of subsheaves jointly surjective on stalks
A sheaf is the filtered colimit of subobjects whose stalks exhaust every stalk
mathlib_searches.results: Generic germ existence, basis germ existence, and existence of filtered sheaf colimits; no finite-generation exhaustion or directed stalk-cover criterion.

Stalk and skyscraper APIs; local Mathlib search finds Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf' and the stalkwise isomorphism criterion. No existing construction of finite-generator abelian subsheaf diagrams.
